subject: Materials Science
title: Nanotoxicology: Are Nanomaterials Safe?
description: Learn Nanotoxicology: Are Nanomaterials Safe? in one minute.

hook.text: A material safe in bulk form can become toxic at the nanoscale — size changes everything, including danger.

buildup.text: Nanoparticles cross cell membranes, enter the bloodstream, even reach the brain — paths closed to larger particles.

discovery.text: Inhaled carbon nanotubes cause asbestos-like lung inflammation in mice — the needle shape triggers immune response.

twist.text: Shape, coating, and surface chemistry matter more than composition — same material, different form, different toxicity.

climax.text: Regulatory frameworks are catching up — the EU now requires nano-specific labeling on cosmetics and food products.

punchline.text: New materials need new safety science — nanotoxicology writes the rulebook.

quiz.question: Why might a nanomaterial be more toxic than the same material in bulk form?
options: Nanoparticles can cross biological barriers and interact with cells in ways larger particles cannot
